function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | • Always obey posted signs; speed cameras and radar are common. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for drivers over 18, but all passengers must buckle. | • Check that children are properly secured before starting the trip. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | • Use a Bluetooth headset or voice‑activated controls. | | **Alcohol & Driving** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is DUI.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | • If you’re drinking, designate a sober driver or use rideshare. | | **Driving Under the Influence of Drugs** | • Prescription drugs that impair driving can lead to DUI charges.
• Marijuana possession is legal, but driving under its influence is illegal. | • Know how medications affect your driving; consult a doctor if unsure. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green = go; yellow = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop.
• Yield signs give right‑of‑way to vehicles already in the intersection. | • Always come to a complete stop at red lights and stop signs. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks. | • Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | • Signal early and check mirrors before changing lanes. | | **School Bus** | • Stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• In Texas, you must stop on both sides of the road. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until it resumes motion. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a proper tow bar and a valid license. | • Keep registration documents in the vehicle. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and timed lots enforce payment. | • Pay meters or use parking apps to avoid tickets. | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Minor infractions (e.g., speeding 5–10 mph over limit) can result in a fine and points on your license.
• Major infractions (e.g., reckless driving) can lead to license suspension and higher fines. | • Maintain a clean driving record to keep insurance rates low. | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergencies** | • Call 911 for emergencies.
• For non‑emergency roadside assistance, use a roadside service or the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) roadside assistance program. | • Keep emergency numbers and a spare tire in the car. | ### Quick Reference - **Speed Limits**: 55 mph (rural interstate), 65 mph (urban interstate), 45 mph (highways), 35 mph (city streets). - **Seat‑Belt**: All occupants must buckle. - **Cell‑Phone**: Hand‑held use prohibited; hands‑free allowed. - **DUI**: 0.08% BAC (or 0.02% for under 21). - **School Bus**: Stop on both sides of the road. - **Parking**: No parking in fire lanes, handicap spots (unless permitted), or on sidewalks. --- #### Resources - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** – State statutes governing traffic laws. - **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement and safety information. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or scenario!
